items.title: [Bug]: Windows /resume deletion hides chat, but it returns after restart (1.4.6)

labels.name: subtype:windows
labels.description: Windows specific issues (e.g., login links, PowerShell statusline)

labels.name: comp:conversations
labels.description: Managing Conversations, Workspace Scoping, Resuming sessions, Branching

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.4.6 (also reproduced on 1.4.5).

### Environment Context

- OS: Windows 11, build 26200
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.6
- CLI: native Windows executable installed through WinGet
- Terminal: used through Orca; independently reproduced through a private terminal session
- Normal existing CLI profile. Other AGY sessions and the Remote Control daemon were running. Their involvement has not been isolated.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `agy` and open `/resume`.
2. Select an old conversation in the CLI list.
3. Press the displayed delete shortcut (`F4` on 1.4.6).
4. Confirm with `y`. The confirmation is accepted and the row disappears.
5. Exit and restart AGY, then open `/resume` again.
6. The same conversation is back.

This is manually reproducible. In an additional controlled test, reopening the picker within the same process was already enough to restore the row; a full restart was unnecessary.

### Expected Behavior

Successful deletion should persist across a fresh picker and restart. If the conversation cannot be deleted, the picker should retain the row and display the failure instead of making it appear deleted.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

The selected row disappears immediately, but the conversation remains on disk and returns to the list.

In the controlled 1.4.6 test:
- The picker count dropped from 39 to 38, then returned to 39 on reopening.
- The exact target database still existed after clean CLI exit, with unchanged size and SHA-256.
- The selected old conversation was not resumed or prompted during the test.
- The native log recorded the error below. The holder of the file has not been identified; this report does not establish that the daemon or another CLI session is the cause.
- The same native picker workflow successfully deleted two test conversations on Debian with 1.4.6 and its daemon left running.

### Logs & Configurations

Sanitized native error (user path and conversation ID replaced):

```text
Failed to delete trajectory <conversation-id>: remove <USERPROFILE>\.gemini\antigravity-cli\conversations\<conversation-id>.db: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
```

No manual database/sidecar deletion was used.

Related issues checked: #139 requests non-interactive deletion; #80 and #732 concern deletion shortcuts. Here the shortcut and confirmation work, but the native file deletion fails and the picker still removes the row. I did not find an existing report of this exact persistence/sharing-error combination.

items.title: [Bug]: Long-running Remote Control daemon misses local conversations until restart, even with matching CLI/daemon 1.4.7

labels.name: subtype:ubuntu/Linux
labels.description: Ubuntu/Linux build, execution, or keybinding issues

labels.name: comp:conversations
labels.description: Managing Conversations, Workspace Scoping, Resuming sessions, Branching

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

Installed CLI: `1.4.7` on both affected hosts. Host A had a stale `1.4.6` daemon after a CLI update. A follow-up check found the same incomplete-index symptom on Host B with **both the installed CLI and running daemon already on 1.4.7**, so version skew is not required.

### Environment Context

- Host A: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x86_64
- Host B: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Linux x86_64
- Shell: bash
- Remote Control: persistent `systemd --user` service, enabled at login/boot
- Service command: `%h/.local/bin/agy remote-control serve`
- Web client: `https://antigravity.google.com`

### Summary

A long-running Remote Control daemon can retain an incomplete conversation summary index while newer CLI conversations exist in local SQLite databases and the regular CLI summary cache. The service remains `active (running)`, and its status does not indicate missing history.

On Host A, this was noticed after a CLI update left the daemon running a replaced executable: recent conversations were missing in Remote Control. One restart switched 1.4.6 to 1.4.7 and rebuilt the daemon cache from 25 to 38 records.

A subsequent audit of Host B found an important control case: the daemon and installed CLI were already both 1.4.7, with no deleted executable, yet its daemon cache contained only 1 of 3 local summary records. One omitted record was a real, nonempty 174-step top-level conversation created/updated after the daemon started. Restarting the same version restored the missing records. Thus this should be investigated as a long-lived summary discovery/reconciliation problem, with updater lifecycle as an additional concern rather than an established sole cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

The sequence below documents Host A. Host B provides a same-version observation in the follow-up section. These are observations from existing installations, not a controlled downgrade/upgrade experiment:

1. Run the persistent daemon with CLI 1.4.6 using `agy remote-control start` / the installed systemd user service.
2. Update the installed CLI to 1.4.7 while the daemon remains running. Automatic CLI updates are used on this machine; the exact invocation that performed this update was not captured.
3. Create/use conversations with the newer CLI over the following days.
4. Open the persistent daemon instance in Remote Control. Recent conversations are missing even though local conversation databases and the newer local summary index contain them.
5. Check the service: it is still active, but `/proc/<daemon-pid>/exe` points to a replaced/deleted old executable and its startup log identifies version 1.4.6.
6. With all indexed conversations idle and no other processes in the service cgroup, run:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user restart antigravity-cli-daemon.service
   ```

7. The new daemon reports version 1.4.7, its executable is no longer deleted, and its Remote Control summary cache now contains all 38 locally indexed records.

### Expected Behavior

The always-on Remote Control daemon should discover conversations created or updated by other local CLI sessions without a manual restart, including when all processes use the same version. CLI updates should not silently leave it with incomplete history.

If a daemon restart is required after an update, the updater/status command should explicitly identify that requirement and the running versus installed versions. Any automatic restart should respect active work.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

Observed on 2026-10-27; timestamps below are UTC+08:00:

| Check | Before restart | After restart |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service started | 2026-10-24 11:01 | 2026-10-27 09:48 |
| Installed CLI version | 1.4.7 | 1.4.7 |
| Daemon startup version | 1.4.6 | 1.4.7 |
| Executable | `agy.<timestamp>.old (deleted)` | current `agy` |
| systemd status | active/running, no automatic restarts | active/running |
| `conversation_summaries.db` rows | 38 | 38 |
| `jetbox_summaries_proto.pb` entries | 38 | 38 |
| `agyhub_summaries_proto.pb` entries | 25 | 38 |

The legacy `cache/conversation_metadata.json` also remained at 26 entries before restart, last modified on October 24. The current binary's mtime was October 24 at 11:07, shortly after the old daemon started.

Protobuf entry counts were checked by parsing the top-level repeated map entries and their conversation UUID keys, then comparing them with the SQLite index. These counts include internal/subagent records; they are not counts of top-level chats in the web UI. Conversation files were preserved.

### Logs & Configurations

Relevant startup/reconciliation lines (personal identifiers omitted):

```text
# Before restart
I1024 11:01:19 ... Language server version: 1.4.6
I1024 11:01:25 ... summary store: starting background reconciliation (trigger=startup)
I1024 11:01:25 ... summary store: reconcile func returned 0 records, skipping

# After restart
I1027 09:48:30 ... Language server version: 1.4.7
I1027 09:48:35 ... summary store: reconciliation complete, synced 25 records
I1027 09:48:36 ... summary store: reconciliation complete, synced 38 records
I1027 09:48:37 ... Connection status: Connected
```

The service uses `Restart=on-failure`; the old daemon had not exited or crashed. `agy remote-control status` reported it as active but did not expose the running/installed version mismatch.

### Scope and related issue

This resembles #1258, which was closed as fixed in 1.4.2, but this observation involves a persistent 1.4.6 daemon alongside installed 1.4.7 and missing *recent* conversations, with a measurable cache repair after restart.

The stale executable and incomplete daemon index were directly observed on Host A. Host B, described below, shows that the index issue can also occur without a version mismatch. Summary reconciliation/file watching in a long-lived daemon is a hypothesis, not a confirmed source-level root cause. After restarting both hosts, their daemon indexes and relay connections were verified; final refreshed browser rendering has not yet been independently verified.


### Follow-up: same-version observation on a second host

Host B was checked over SSH on 2026-10-27. Its persistent daemon had been running since October 24 at 13:26. The installed CLI and daemon startup log both reported `1.4.7`; `/proc/<pid>/exe` still pointed to the current executable, without `(deleted)`.

| Check | Before restart | After restart |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installed CLI / daemon version | 1.4.7 / 1.4.7 | 1.4.7 / 1.4.7 |
| `conversation_summaries.db` rows | 3 | 3 |
| `jetbox_summaries_proto.pb` entries | 3 | 3 |
| `agyhub_summaries_proto.pb` entries | 1 | 3 |
| Nonempty top-level conversations missing from daemon cache | 1 (174 steps) | 0 |

The other missing record was an empty placeholder, so the count is not being presented as two missing substantive chats. The nonempty missing conversation had a last-modified time of October 24 at 15:30, after daemon startup.

All indexed records were idle, and the daemon had no child processes, before restarting. No CLI update, cache deletion, configuration change, or conversation edit was needed. The same service was restarted with `systemctl --user restart antigravity-cli-daemon.service`.

Startup was slow because authentication/configuration requests took time, but it completed. The new log explicitly corroborates the index repair:

```text
I1027 09:51:02 ... Language server version: 1.4.7
I1027 09:52:19 ... [Summaries] reconcile checked 3 conversations, restored 2, cached 1, skipped 0, dropped 0, cancelled false in 219ms (resident: 0 -> 0)
I1027 09:52:19 ... summary store: reconciliation complete, synced 3 records
I1027 09:52:29 ... Connection status: Connected
```

The second host's missing record was verified in the local daemon summary artifact, not independently through its browser UI. This additional observation narrows the report: automatic updates/version skew are **not necessary** for a long-running daemon to retain an incomplete conversation index.

items.body:
After updating Antigravity (Windows), all previously working MCP server connections broke with a persistent "Failed to load MCP servers" error in Customizations → Installed MCP Servers.

Steps observed:

1. Had 2 working MCP servers configured in C:\Users\<user>\.gemini\config\mcp_config.json (custom HTTP MCP servers using serverUrl + headers for auth).
2. Updated Antigravity to the latest version.
3. Update process created a .migrated marker file and a new config.json (containing userSettings.globalPermissionGrants) in the same config folder.
4. mcp_config.json became a .symlink with Attributes: Archive, ReparsePoint, 0 bytes.
5. Checked the symlink's target with Get-Item ... | Select-Object Target — it points to itself (mcp_config.json → mcp_config.json), a broken circular reference.
6. A second copy of mcp_config.json was found at .gemini\antigravity\mcp_config.json — also 0 bytes, also a broken ReparsePoint.
7. Deleted both broken symlinks, and also deleted the entire .gemini\antigravity\mcp cache folder, then fully restarted Antigravity (killed all processes via Task Manager, not just closed the window).
8. Error persists identically after full deletion and restart — "Failed to load MCP servers" with no server list shown.
9. Checked .gemini\antigravity\crashes\ for a relevant crash log from the same timestamp — the log file exists but is   
0 bytes, so no diagnostic info is available client-side.

Expected: Either the migration should correctly carry forward existing MCP server configs, or at minimum not leave a broken self-referencing symlink with no recovery path or error detail.

Actual: MCP servers are completely unusable post-update, with no actionable error message and an empty crash log.

Environment: Windows, Antigravity (updated today — [2.19.1]).

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.3.4

### Environment Context

- OS: Windows 10
- Shell: PowerShell invoking cmd.exe
- Application: Antigravity CLI (agy)
- Incident date: October 14, 2026
- Timezone: WIB (UTC+7)
- Restore point: Not available

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows 10, I asked the Antigravity CLI agent to clean unnecessary files on drive C: to free up disk space.
2. During cleanup, the agent attempted to remove leftover CapCut and Postman directories.
3. The agent generated recursive deletion commands using cmd.exe /c and rmdir /s /q, with backslash-escaped quotation marks.
4. At steps 326–327, the execution log unexpectedly included thousands of paths outside the intended application directories.
5. After the operation, multiple applications stopped working and PowerShell could no longer be launched normally.

WARNING: These steps describe a recorded incident. Do not reproduce the destructive commands on a real system.

### Expected Behavior

The agent should delete only files and directories explicitly validated as safe cleanup targets. Recursive deletion commands must never operate outside the intended paths, especially on Windows system directories, Program Files, user data, or the root of a drive. Potentially destructive commands should require strict path validation and explicit user confirmation.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

The agent unexpectedly attempted recursive deletion across directories outside the intended cleanup targets.

Technical evidence:
- Suspicious execution recorded at steps 326–327.
- task-327.log contains 38,271 output lines.
- Over 35,000 lines reference Program Files paths.
- Other output references Windows files and user directories.
- Command exit code: -1073741510.
- The CLI later failed to write its own log because a path could not be found.

Observed damage:
- Multiple installed applications stopped launching.
- PowerShell could not be launched normally.
- Several application executables were reported missing.
- No Windows System Restore point was available.

The execution output strongly suggests unintended recursive traversal of drive C:. The exact number of successfully deleted files remains unknown.

### Logs & Configurations

Relevant evidence is preserved locally:
- Antigravity conversation database, steps 326–327
- task-327.log
- CLI execution logs
- Full session transcript

The original logs may contain personal information and sensitive paths, so they are not publicly attached.

Please provide a private channel to submit the complete logs securely.

Potentially related incident: #459
https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/issues/459

I request that this incident be escalated to the engineering and safety teams for investigation of recursive deletion safeguards and Windows command-line quoting.

items.title: [Security] OS Command Injection in Gemini Antigravity CLI via Unsanitized Input Evaluation

labels.name: security
labels.description: To flag token exposure or internal instruction leaks

items.body:
## Vulnerability Description

An OS Command Injection vulnerability has been identified in **Google Anitgravity CLI 1.0.0** due to the unsafe use of the `eval` shell command. The payload/script natively processes user-supplied input provided via the primary command-line argument (`$1`) and interpolates it directly into an active evaluation execution scope without any prior sanitization, validation, or encapsulation boundaries. This happens because Google Antigravity CLI validates top-level run_shell_command calls like rm, ls, and others, and applies restrictions through prefix matching and command splitting. 



**Attack Preconditions**

To exploit this vulnerability, the following conditions must be met:

A vuln.sh script exists in the repository that takes unvalidated input and runs it using `eval`. *The script is executed by Google Anitgravity CLI using something like: (e.g., through an exposed backend utility, an infrastructure webhook, a task queue worker, or an internal CI/CD build pipeline configuration).*

Vulnerable Script

```
#!/bin/bash
echo "Welcome!"
echo "You entered: $1"
eval "$1"

# Run rm -rf on $2 (second argument)
rm -rf "$2"
echo "Deleted $2"
```


* The script must be actively deployed on the hosting system with local executable privileges.



**Reproduction Steps / POC**

1. Deploy the target script at any location /tmp , (`vuln.sh`) to the test environment and ensure it has proper executable permissions:


```bash
chmod +x vuln.sh

```


2. Execute the script from the terminal, supplying an argument string that contains a benign command followed by a chain control delimiter (`&&`) and a secondary test payload (e.g., a local utility process invocation):



```bash
   ./vuln.sh "echo hello && calc.exe"

```
3. Observe the system execution standard output log to confirm arbitrary processing:



```text
   Welcome!
   You entered: echo hello && calc.exe
   hello
   Deleted 

```

*PoC Analysis:* The video reproduction output explicitly demonstrates that the runtime shell successfully processed the initial `echo hello` directive and natively evaluated the trailing `calc.exe` pop-up command string expression within the executing environment context.

```
Payloads 

# System info extraction
./vuln.sh "echo $(uname -a)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(hostname)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(id)"

# Nested substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(echo $(whoami)@$(hostname))"

# File read via substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(cat /etc/hostname)"

# Environment leak
./vuln.sh "echo $(env)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(printenv HOME)"

# Process listing
./vuln.sh "echo $(ps aux)"

# Network info
./vuln.sh "echo $(ifconfig)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(ip addr)"

# Backtick variant (same effect)
./vuln.sh "echo `whoami`"
./vuln.sh "echo `id`"

# Double nested
./vuln.sh "echo $($(echo whoami))"

# Substitution + chaining
./vuln.sh "echo $(whoami && hostname && id)"

# Write output to file via substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(whoami > /tmp/out.txt)"

# Base64 encoded command inside substitution
./vuln.sh "echo $(echo d2hvYW1p | base64 -d | bash)"

./vuln.sh "echo $(cmd.exe /c whoami)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(powershell -c Get-Process)"
./vuln.sh "echo $(cmd.exe /c systeminfo)"


## Security Risk 

1. *eval on unsanitized input = full system compromise. There is no partial exploitation — once an attacker can inject into eval, they have the same access as the running process. If that process runs as root or has cloud IAM roles, the blast radius extends to the entire infrastructure.*
2. Supply Chain Attack  - Any threat actor capable of interacting with the upstream interface or asset that pipes data into the first command-line argument ($1) of the vuln.sh script. Depending on how this script is integrated, this could range from an unauthenticated remote attacker (if exposed via a public-facing web hook, API endpoint, or form parameter) to a lower-privileged internal user or automated service account (if utilized within an internal task queue worker or CI/CD deployment pipeline configuration).

items.title: [Bug]: Importing desktop conversation destructively overwrites original session summary in ~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db
items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.2.2

### Environment Context

- **OS:** Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26100)
- **Terminal Emulator:** Windows Terminal (PowerShell)
- **Runtime Version:** Antigravity Desktop 2.0 (v2.13.0) + Antigravity CLI 1.2.2
- **Hardware Details:** AMD64 (x86_64)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an active conversation in Antigravity Desktop.
2. Open Antigravity CLI (`agy`).
3. In CLI prompt, run `/resume` to open the Session Picker.
4. Press `Tab` to switch to the `Other` tab.
5. Highlight the desktop conversation and press `Enter`.
6. Confirm import: `[Import this conversation? (y/n)]` -> `y`.

### Expected Behavior

The CLI should import the conversation non-destructively:
- Read the desktop conversation as read-only.
- Create an isolated fork session in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<fork_id>.db`.
- Register the summary only in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db`.
- Leave the original conversation and its summary in `~/.gemini/antigravity/` completely untouched.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

During import, the CLI's language server backend mutates the **Desktop** summary store (`~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db` and `agyhub_summaries_proto.pb`) for ANY imported conversation:
1. In `~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db`, the existing row for the source conversation has its:
   - `conversation_id` replaced by `<fork_id>`
   - `title` cleared to empty string `""`
   - `project_id` unconditionally altered to `default-cli-project` (destroying both project affiliations and `outside-of-project` status)
   - `workspace_uris` changed to `["file:///C:/Users/..."]`
   - `source` changed to `CORTEX_TRAJECTORY_SOURCE_CLI`
2. As a consequence:
   - The conversation completely disappears from the left sidebar of Antigravity Desktop and Remote Control (both from project lists and from the "Outside of Project" Conversations list).
   - It is not displayed under "CLI Project" in Desktop either due to the empty title and CLI source filter.
   - The underlying database file `~/.gemini/antigravity/conversations/<original_id>.db` is NOT deleted, so navigating via direct URL (`/r/<install_id>?p=<original_id>`) still loads all steps, but it shows as "Untitled Conversation" because the summary index record is orphaned.

### Logs & Configurations

From CLI log (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log`):
```log
I0912 15:02:42.591813     488 server.go:3201] Importing conversation <original_id> from antigravity
I0912 15:02:42.599577     488 server.go:2306] Forking conversation from <original_id> (agentOverride=false)
I0912 15:02:42.677501     488 server.go:2367] Forked conversation <original_id> -> <fork_id>
E0912 15:02:42.688130     488 errorreport.go:224] trajectory <fork_id> already loaded, skipping duplicate load
```

Database record mutation observed in `~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db`:
```yaml
Before import:
  conversation_id: <original_id>
  title: "<original_title>"
  project_id: "<original_project_id>" # (or "outside-of-project")

After import:
  conversation_id: <fork_id>
  title: ""
  project_id: "default-cli-project"
  source: "CORTEX_TRAJECTORY_SOURCE_CLI"
```

labels.name: others

items.body:
I experienced catastrophic data loss while running AGY with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

A repository contained a directory named `nul`. I asked AGY to remove it from Git. AGY attempted to execute:

```cmd
rd /s /q "\\?\C:\...\Projects\nul"
```

Because `nul` is a special Windows device name, Windows may normalize the path unexpectedly. In my case, the operation appears to have been interpreted as:

```cmd
rd /s /q "\\?\C:"
```

As a result, AGY recursively deleted almost everything it had permission to delete on my C: drive.

This issue is especially dangerous because:

* `nul`, `con`, `prn`, `aux`, etc. are well-known reserved Windows device names.
* AGY executed a recursive delete without validating the target path.
* Even after pressing `Esc`, the previous task continued running in the background.
* The consequence was complete data loss rather than a repository-local failure.

AGY should never perform destructive operations involving Windows reserved device names without additional safeguards and explicit path validation.

items.title: [Bug] Windows startup reports “not signed in” before valid keyring auth completes (~5.6s race)
items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `agy` can start by showing:

```text
Welcome to the Antigravity CLI. You are currently not signed in.
```

even though a valid Antigravity credential is already present in Windows Credential Manager and the CLI successfully authenticates from that keyring a few seconds later.

This appears to be a startup auth-state race / delayed state propagation rather than credential loss: token-dependent components begin running while authentication is still unresolved and repeatedly observe `You are not logged into Antigravity.` before `ChainedAuth` finishes.

## Environment

* Antigravity CLI: **1.1.22**
* OS: **Windows**
* Shell: **PowerShell**
* Binary: `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\agy\bin\agy.exe`
* Only one `agy.exe` is resolved by `Get-Command agy -All`
* Profile/state directory: `C:\Users\Administrator\.gemini\antigravity-cli`

## Credential state

Before starting the CLI, Windows Credential Manager contains:

```text
Target: LegacyGeneric:target=gemini:antigravity
Type: Generic
User: antigravity
Persistence: Local machine
```

So the credential is persisted and available to the same Windows environment.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to Antigravity successfully once.
2. Confirm `LegacyGeneric:target=gemini:antigravity` exists in Windows Credential Manager.
3. Close the CLI / terminal.
4. Open a new PowerShell session.
5. Run `agy`.
6. Observe that the CLI initially reports that the user is not signed in.
7. Inspect `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/cli.log`.

## Actual behavior

At startup, multiple subsystems immediately attempt authenticated operations and fail with `You are not logged into Antigravity.`:

```text
11:20:09.935  Failed to poll ListExperiments: error getting token source:
               You are not logged into Antigravity.

11:20:09.938  Cache(loadCodeAssistResponse): Singleflight refresh failed:
               error getting token source: You are not logged into Antigravity.

11:20:09.974  quota_manager.go: doRefreshQuota: skipped (not logged in)
```

However, only milliseconds later the keyring loader confirms that a valid, non-expired token was successfully loaded:

```text
11:20:09.989  keyring.go:81] keyringAuth: loaded token,
               expiry=2026-09-01 12:16:54 +0800, expired=false
```

Then about **5.64 seconds later**, authentication completes successfully using that same keyring credential:

```text
11:20:15.632  auth.go:147] ChainedAuth: authenticated via keyring (effective: keyring)
11:20:15.632  server_oauth.go:195] OAuth: authenticated successfully as <redacted>
```

There is also a suspicious intermediate state where one component reports success while other components still see no token source:

```text
11:20:09.957  server.go:2853] Auth succeeded, refreshing features and managers

11:20:09.957  Failed to poll ListExperiments: error getting token source:
               You are not logged into Antigravity.
```

This makes the startup auth state appear internally inconsistent.

## Expected behavior

When a valid persisted keyring credential exists:

1. The CLI should not display a definitive **“You are currently not signed in”** state while keyring authentication is still pending.
2. Components that require authentication should either wait until `ChainedAuth` resolves or receive an explicit `auth pending` state instead of `not logged in`.
3. If startup authentication eventually succeeds from the keyring, no login prompt / unauthenticated state should be surfaced to the user as if credentials were missing.

An optimistic/non-blocking UI is also fine, but it should represent the state as **Signing in / Restoring session**, not **Not signed in**.

## Why this appears different from existing issues

* #88 reported login state not being persisted and was closed as fixed in 1.0.1. In this case the credential **is persisted and successfully loaded**.
* #494 requests non-blocking/optimistic sign-in because of startup latency. This report adds evidence of an internal auth-state race where subsystems incorrectly observe `not logged in` before authentication resolves.
* #523 reports intermittent OAuth token exchange/network failure on Windows. In this case there is **no token exchange failure** in the captured session; keyring authentication succeeds.

## Possible root cause

The startup sequence appears to expose a default unauthenticated state before asynchronous keyring / `ChainedAuth` initialization has completed:

```text
startup
  -> auth-dependent caches/managers initialize
  -> current auth state == not logged in
  -> UI/subsystems surface unauthenticated errors
  -> keyringAuth loads valid token
  -> ChainedAuth continues validation
  -> ~5.6s later auth result is applied
```

Potential fixes could include:

* introduce an explicit `auth pending / restoring session` state;
* defer auth-dependent cache/quota/experiment initialization until the initial auth attempt resolves;
* avoid rendering `not signed in` unless the initial keyring/ChainedAuth attempt actually fails;
* or make startup optimistic while authentication proceeds in the background, similar to #494.

## Additional diagnostics

The issue reproduces with a single installed `agy.exe`; no multi-version PATH conflict was found. The Windows credential is present and marked with local-machine persistence.

A larger sanitized `cli.log` excerpt can be provided if useful.

items.title: [Bug]: [IDE] GitHub Pull Requests/Actions extensions lose auth session on every restart — race condition in secret storage startup

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

Not an agy CLI issue — this is the Antigravity IDE. Version info from the IDE's About dialog:  Antigravity IDE Version: 2.5.5 VSCode OSS Version: 1.107.0 Commit: ecfbad74d93962fc8ca485d93ab9b4f3d4cb6cf8 Date: 2026-08-13T08:37:22.547Z Electron: 39.2.3 Chromium: 142.0.7444.175 Node.js: 22.21.1 V8: 14.2.231.21-electron.0 OS: Linux x64 7.0.0-31-generic snap Language Server CL: 963923152  Filing here because google-antigravity has no public repo for the IDE itself. Already submitted via the in-app Feedback tool; posting here too for visibility, since the underlying ~/.gemini auth infrastructure is shared and this repo has active engineering eyes on it. Apologies if this needs redirecting — happy to close if there's a better venue.

### Environment Context

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, X11
- Kernel: 7.0.0-31-generic
- Installation: Ubuntu App Store (Snap), package antigravity-ide-snap, revision 6, classic confinement
- GitHub Pull Requests extension: 0.114.3
- GitHub Actions extension: 0.32.3 (github.vscode-github-actions)
- Git: 2.43.0
- GNOME Keyring: installed, daemon running (--components=pkcs11,secrets), confirmed functional via manual secret-tool store/lookup/clear round trip
- gh CLI: authenticates and persists fine across restarts using the same system keyring (gh auth status confirms "✓ Logged in ... (keyring)")

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Quit Antigravity fully, confirm no process remains: `ps aux | grep antigravity`
2. Launch Antigravity, open the GitHub Pull Requests panel, sign in with a GitHub account (repo, workflow scopes).
3. Confirm the session is stored:
   sqlite3 "$HOME/.config/Antigravity IDE/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb" \
     "SELECT key, length(value) FROM ItemTable WHERE key LIKE 'secret://%';"
   Expect a row like: secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709
4. Quit Antigravity fully via the UI, confirm no process remains. Re-run the query — row still present (token survives shutdown intact).
5. Relaunch Antigravity. Without touching anything, wait a few seconds, then re-run the query — the row is now gone.
6. Open View → Output → "GitHub Authentication" channel — see `Reading sessions from keychain...` / `Got 0 sessions` logged ~227ms after the process's first log line.
7. Open View → Output → "GitHub Actions" channel — see `Cannot fetch github context` errors.
8. Both the Pull Requests and Actions panels now show signed out, requiring re-authentication.

### Expected Behavior

The GitHub session should persist across Antigravity restarts, matching the behavior of gh CLI, git (via credential helper), and the IDE's general account sign-in — all of which remain authenticated across restarts on the same machine and same GitHub account.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

The GitHub Pull Requests and GitHub Actions extensions lose their authenticated session on every restart, even though the underlying secret is confirmed to be written correctly and to survive shutdown. Root cause traced via direct inspection of state.vscdb (full detail below in Logs).

GitHub Actions extension error:

Cannot fetch github context
Error: Cannot fetch github context
    at De (/home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1200371)
    at async /home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1404017
    at async Ls (/home/prime/.antigravity-ide/extensions/github.vscode-github-actions-0.32.3-universal/dist/extension-node.js:1:1403089)
    at async e9._activate (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:17036)
    at async e9._waitForDepsThenActivate (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:16978)
    at async e9._initialize (file:///snap/antigravity-ide-snap/6/usr/share/antigravity-ide/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js:120:16341)

GitHub Authentication channel (fresh launch):

[info] Reading sessions from keychain...
[info] Getting sessions for all scopes...
[info] Got 0 sessions for ...
[info] Getting sessions for repo,workflow...
[info] Got 0 sessions for repo,workflow...

### Logs & Configurations

Root cause, confirmed via direct database inspection:

1. After signing in, the encrypted session is written to state.vscdb as
   secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"} (~709 bytes).
2. This row survives a full app shutdown intact — confirmed by querying the DB
   immediately after quitting.
3. On the next launch, the row is still present immediately after startup, then is
   silently deleted a few seconds later while the app is idle, before any user
   interaction.
4. 227ms is implausibly fast for a genuine Linux secret-storage read, which requires
   a D-Bus round trip to gnome-keyring-daemon — more so under this Snap's classic
   confinement, which adds an extra D-Bus proxy hop. Likely mechanism: the GitHub
   Authentication provider attempts to decrypt the stored session before Electron's
   safeStorage Linux backend has finished initializing; the decrypt fails, and VS
   Code core's secret-storage self-healing logic treats the entry as corrupted and
   deletes it rather than retrying once the backend is actually ready.

Ruled out as causes:
- GNOME Keyring/libsecret — confirmed functional via manual secret-tool round trip,
  and gh auth status persists fine across restarts using the same keyring.
- libssl1.1 — confirmed installed via ldconfig -p | grep libssl.so.1.1, no change
  in behavior.
- "password-store": "gnome-libsecret" forced in argv.json — no change.
- encryption.migratedToGnomeLibsecret flag — already `true` and stable across
  restarts, ruling out a re-migration loop.

state.vscdb query outputs (chronological):

# Right after sign-in:
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# Immediately after full shutdown (process confirmed gone via ps aux):
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# Immediately after next relaunch:
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"}|709

# A few seconds later, app idle, no interaction:
(empty result — row deleted)

Happy to attach the full raw logs as a file if the form supports it.

items.title: [Bug]: All models gated behind a retired "Gemini Code Assist for individuals" eligibility check - verdict differs between two accounts at the same location

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

items.body:
### Antigravity CLI Version

1.2.2

### Environment Context

- **OS:** Windows 11 Home 25H2, 10.0.26200 (Build 26200), 64-bit
- **Shell:** PowerShell 7.6.5 (also reproduces under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash - shell-independent)
- **Terminal Emulator:** Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 (also reproduces non-interactively via `--print`)
- **Runtime Version:** Antigravity CLI (`agy`) 1.2.2; Antigravity IDE 1.107.0, quality `stable`, commit `ecfbad74d93962fc8ca485d93ab9b4f3d4cb6cf8`, built 2026-08-13
- **Hardware Details:** Intel Core i7-1360P (12C/16T), 32 GB RAM, x86_64. Residential ISP, single IPv4 egress, no routable IPv6, `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` unset.

Auth: consumer Google account (personal Gmail, not Workspace). Two independent consumer accounts were tested - referred to below as Account A and Account B.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to Antigravity with a consumer Google account (Account A).
2. Run any Gemini model non-interactively:
   `agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"`
   -> `error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.`
3. Run the same prompt on a non-Gemini model, same session, same account, same IP:
   `agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"`
   -> returns `OK` normally.
4. Re-run step 2 against the production Cloud Code backend instead of the default:
   `CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"`
   -> the location error is **gone**; returns `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429)` instead.
5. Sign out, sign in with a second independent consumer account (Account B) on the same machine, repeat step 2.
   -> a different error, and now **every** model fails, including `claude-sonnet-4-6`:
   `Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.`

Tip: set `AGY_CLI_MODEL_API_MAX_RETRIES=0` to skip the retry backoff and surface the error immediately.


### Expected Behavior

Antigravity should not gate its own models behind the eligibility rules of **Gemini Code Assist for individuals** - a product retired on 2026-06-18 whose documented migration target is Antigravity itself (https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/resources/available-locations).

And whatever gate does apply should be consistent: the same verdict for two consumer accounts at the same location, and the same verdict across backends for one account.

### Actual Behavior / Error Screenshots

Every request is gated by an eligibility check for **"Gemini Code Assist for individuals"**, a product that stopped serving requests on 2026-06-18 and whose stated migration path *is Antigravity*. Antigravity appears to still enforce the retired product's location eligibility gate.

Two independent consumer accounts, same machine, same IP, minutes apart:

| | Account A | Account B |
|---|---|---|
| Eligibility check | passes | **blocked** - "not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location" |
| Gemini, default backend (`daily-cloudcode-pa`) | `400 FAILED_PRECONDITION` - "User location is not supported for the API use" | eligibility error |
| Claude (`claude-sonnet-4-6`), default backend | **`200` OK** | eligibility error |
| Gemini, production backend (`cloudcode-pa` via `CLOUD_CODE_URL`) | `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` - no location error | eligibility error |

Two distinct problems are visible:

1. **The gate is account-scoped, not region-scoped.** Two consumer accounts on the same machine and IP get different verdicts. Account A is served normally on non-Gemini models; Account B is refused every model. A location-based restriction should not differ between two accounts at one location.
2. **Account A's failure is inconsistent across backends.** The same account and IP produce a location precondition failure on the daily backend, but a plain quota error with no location complaint on production.

Verbatim transcript, Account A (`AGY_CLI_MODEL_API_MAX_RETRIES=0`):

```console
$ agy --version
1.2.2

$ agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model gemini-3.1-pro-low -p "say OK"
error: FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.

$ agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
OK

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota).

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
error: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota).
```

Verbatim transcript, Account B, same machine, same IP, minutes later:

```console
$ agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.

$ agy --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.

$ CLOUD_CODE_URL=https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com agy --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"
error: Your current account is not eligible for Gemini Code Assist for individuals because it is not currently available in your location.
```

### Secondary bug: eligibility check hard-fails on an IPv6-only avatar fetch

On a machine with no routable IPv6, the first run after signing in fails outright:

```
error: Eligibility check failed: failed to get profile picture:
Get "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/...=s96-c":
dial tcp [2404:6800:4005:826::2001]:443: connectex: A connection attempt failed ...
```

The eligibility check resolves the avatar URL to IPv6 only with no IPv4 fallback, blocking the entire session on a cosmetic asset. Subsequent runs get past it.

### Things ruled out

- **Not a VPN, proxy or geo-IP spoofing artifact.** Egress is a single plain residential IPv4 (verified against an IP geolocation service), no IPv6 route, `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` unset. Whatever the correct location verdict is, it is applied inconsistently: two accounts at one location get different answers, and one account gets different answers from two backends.
- **`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` has no effect.** Setting it does not populate the quota project - `applyAuthResult` still logs `quotaProject=` (empty). The CLI appears not to forward it as `x-goog-user-project`.
- **Not fixed by switching accounts.** The second consumer account is refused *more* broadly, not less.
- **Not fixed by updating or re-authenticating.** `agy update` reports no version newer than 1.2.2; signing out and back in via the IDE changes nothing.
- **Not CLI-only.** The same failure occurs in the Antigravity IDE agent, consistent with a shared backend route.

### Workaround

For Account A only: non-Gemini models (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-6-thinking`) work on the default backend. There is no workaround for Account B - every model is refused at the eligibility gate. Forcing the production backend with `CLOUD_CODE_URL` removes the location error but yields `429`, so it is evidence rather than a workaround.

### Related

#291 - same symptom, but attributed there to a geographic restriction.

### Logs & Configurations

From `agy --log-file ./agy.log --model gemini-3.8-flash-low -p "say OK"` (Account A):

```
server_oauth.go:192] applyAuthResult: email=<redacted>, authMethod=consumer, quotaProject=
http_helpers.go:299] URL: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:loadCodeAssist
http_helpers.go:299] URL: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:fetchAvailableModels
server.go:1145]      Conversation using project ID: default-cli-project
server.go:2091]      Backend project ID updated dynamically to: default-cli-project
errorreport.go:224]  agent executor error: generating and executing:
                     FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 400): User location is not supported for the API use.
```

Note `quotaProject=` is **empty**, matching the account-provisioning reports where the backend fails to associate a Cloud Project ID and surfaces the failure as a location error.

The log line for Account B has the identical shape (`authMethod=consumer, quotaProject=` empty), so the two accounts are not distinguishable by anything visible client-side.

Error IDs:

```
10373e5b-4364-422f-b901-ec8dcee4abda-1
c86d1bcc-388c-4969-89a2-f0eed172c1fd-1
```

No custom configuration: no proxy env vars, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` unset (and ignored when set), default backend host, no MCP servers configured for these runs.

items.title: Google Antigravity CLI — Preliminary Incident Report
items.body:
# Google Antigravity CLI — Preliminary Incident Report

**Incident Type:** Excessive / Unexpected Disk Consumption
**Affected Environment:** macOS
**Tool:** Google Antigravity CLI / AGY
**Report Status:** Preliminary — forensic evidence collection pending
**Date of Incident Report:** 24-09-2026

---

## 1. Executive Summary

During use of Google Antigravity CLI (AGY) on a macOS system, the available disk space decreased dramatically during an AGY session.

Before the incident, approximately **140 GB of free disk space** was available.

During the incident, AGY began creating files at a rate and/or volume that was sufficiently large to reduce available free space to approximately **10 GB**.

The user terminated AGY after observing abnormal behavior and rapidly increasing disk consumption.

The user states that the AGY environment was being operated with a **sandbox environment enabled**.

The exact files, directories, timestamps, aggregate size, and mechanism responsible for the disk consumption have **not yet been independently established** and must be determined through forensic inspection of the affected machine.

No deletion or cleanup should be performed until the relevant evidence has been inventoried.

---

## 2. Primary Concern

The principal concern is not merely that AGY generated files.

The concern is that an AGY-controlled execution environment apparently permitted or resulted in the generation of an unexpectedly large quantity of persistent data despite the user's understanding that the environment was sandboxed.

The incident therefore raises questions concerning:

1. What data was generated?
2. Where was it generated?
3. When was it generated?
4. How much data was generated?
5. Which AGY process or subprocess generated it?
6. Why was the data generated?
7. Was the data expected runtime state, cache, temporary data, project output, logs, artifacts, database state, or another category?
8. Why was there no effective disk-consumption safeguard preventing the system from approaching exhaustion?
9. Did the sandbox constrain filesystem location but not storage consumption?
10. Did any AGY process or subprocess continue writing unexpectedly or enter a repeated execution loop?

---

## 3. Relevant Google Documentation

Google's current Antigravity documentation describes the Terminal Sandbox as an OS-level isolation mechanism.

For macOS, Google states that Antigravity uses `sandbox-exec` / Seatbelt to restrict filesystem access and socket connections.

Google also states that sandboxed commands can write to:

* project folders;
* temporary directories;
* common build caches.

Therefore, the existence of a sandbox does not by itself establish that the agent is subject to a disk-space quota.

Google's documentation also describes filesystem permissions and workspace access separately from the terminal sandbox.

These distinctions are relevant to this incident because filesystem isolation and resource-consumption limits are different security properties.

---

## 4. User Environment Observation

The user reports:

**Initial available disk space:** approximately 140 GB

**Available disk space after abnormal AGY activity:** approximately 10 GB

**Approximate apparent change:** approximately 130 GB

This figure is an observation supplied by the user and should be verified against filesystem/system records where possible.

The user stopped AGY after observing the abnormal behavior.

---

## 5. Sandbox Context

The user reports that AGY was operating inside a sandbox environment.

This is significant because the user's expectation was that the sandbox would provide meaningful containment against harmful filesystem behavior.

Google's documentation confirms that Antigravity provides a Terminal Sandbox and describes filesystem restrictions for sandboxed execution.

However, Google's documentation does not, in the material reviewed for this report, establish that the sandbox imposes a maximum disk-usage quota for agent-generated files.

Therefore:

**Sandbox enabled ≠ proven disk-resource containment.**

This distinction should be explicitly investigated.

---

## 6. Evidence That Must Be Collected

Before deleting or modifying suspicious data, the following evidence should be captured.

### 6.1 Filesystem Evidence

For every potentially AGY-generated location:

* absolute path;
* filename;
* file type;
* creation time;
* modification time;
* access time where available;
* file size;
* directory aggregate size;
* number of files;
* directory hierarchy.

### 6.2 AGY Evidence

Collect:

* AGY version;
* AGY CLI configuration;
* sandbox configuration;
* permission configuration;
* execution mode;
* session identifiers;
* session logs;
* agent logs;
* subprocess information;
* generated artifacts;
* internal state directories;
* temporary directories associated with AGY;
* database files;
* SQLite WAL/journal files;
* caches;
* backup directories.

### 6.3 Temporal Correlation

The investigation should establish:

```text
AGY SESSION START
        ↓
FIRST UNUSUAL FILE CREATION
        ↓
RAPID FILE GROWTH
        ↓
DISK SPACE DECREASE
        ↓
AGY TERMINATED
        ↓
FILE GROWTH STOPPED?
```

Creation and modification timestamps should be compared against the exact AGY session period.

---

## 7. Important Preliminary Hypothesis

There are publicly documented reports involving unusually large Antigravity/AGY state directories and excessive disk usage.

These reports are **not evidence that the present incident has the same cause**.

They are relevant investigative leads only.

The present incident must be independently verified from the affected machine.

Potential categories to investigate include:

```text
~/.gemini/
    antigravity/
    antigravity-cli/
    antigravity-ide/
    antigravity-backup/

project workspace
temporary directories
build caches
agent artifacts
session state
logs
SQLite databases
SQLite WAL files
generated files
repeated/orphaned sessions
```

These locations are investigative targets, not confirmed locations of the user's data.

---

## 8. No Destructive Remediation Yet

No suspicious files should be deleted merely because:

* their names are unfamiliar;
* they are inside `.gemini`;
* they appear to be caches;
* they are large;
* they were created during an AGY session.

The evidence should first be preserved.

The initial investigation must be **read-only**.

Only after the files have been identified and their function understood should cleanup or recovery be considered.

---

## 9. Questions for Google

The following questions should be answered by the Antigravity team.

### Question 1 — Disk Resource Limits

Does the Antigravity Terminal Sandbox impose any hard limit on:

* disk space consumed;
* number of files;
* total filesystem writes;
* temporary storage;
* cache size;
* per-session storage?

If not, why is disk-resource exhaustion not protected against by default?

### Question 2 — Persistent Agent State

Which directories are intentionally used by AGY for:

* session state;
* agent memory;
* artifacts;
* backups;
* logs;
* caches;
* databases;
* subprocess state?

What are their expected retention policies?

### Question 3 — Automatic Cleanup

Does AGY automatically remove obsolete:

* session state;
* abandoned sessions;
* temporary files;
* artifacts;
* cache entries;
* SQLite WAL/journal files?

If so, what triggers cleanup?

### Question 4 — Repeated Generation

Can a failed, interrupted, or repeatedly restarted agent session generate duplicate persistent state?

Can an agent or subagent enter a loop that continuously creates files?

### Question 5 — Sandbox Scope

When the Terminal Sandbox is enabled on macOS, exactly which filesystem locations remain writable?

Does the sandbox restrict only **where** data may be written, or does it also restrict **how much** data may be written?

### Question 6 — Subagents

Can spawned subagents independently create persistent state, artifacts, logs, or temporary files?

If so, are those resources accounted against the parent session?

### Question 7 — Disk Exhaustion Protection

What mechanism prevents Antigravity from consuming enough storage to destabilize the host operating system?

If no such mechanism exists, this should be clearly documented as a known limitation.

---

## 10. Severity Assessment

The final severity classification should be made after forensic verification.

At present, the incident should be treated as:

**Potentially serious host-resource exhaustion incident.**

The basis is the reported reduction of approximately 130 GB of available storage during an AGY session.

This classification does not assert malicious behavior.

It also does not establish whether the incident resulted from:

* a software defect;
* runaway agent behavior;
* repeated session generation;
* cache accumulation;
* artifact generation;
* logging;
* database growth;
* temporary files;
* configuration;
* permission behavior;
* or another mechanism.

Those questions remain open pending evidence.

---

## 11. Required Forensic Procedure

The investigation should proceed in this order:

```text
1. STOP AGY
       ↓
2. PRESERVE CURRENT STATE
       ↓
3. RECORD CURRENT FREE SPACE
       ↓
4. IDENTIFY LARGEST DIRECTORIES
       ↓
5. IDENTIFY LARGEST FILES
       ↓
6. IDENTIFY AGY-RELATED LOCATIONS
       ↓
7. RECORD CREATION / MODIFICATION TIMES
       ↓
8. CORRELATE WITH AGY SESSION
       ↓
9. CALCULATE TOTAL GENERATED DATA
       ↓
10. CLASSIFY THE DATA
       ↓
11. PRESERVE EVIDENCE
       ↓
12. ONLY THEN CONSIDER CLEANUP
```

No destructive operation should occur during steps 1–10.

---

## 12. Evidence Status

### Confirmed / User-Reported

* AGY was running on macOS.
* Approximately 140 GB of free disk space was available before the incident.
* Free space subsequently fell to approximately 10 GB.
* AGY began exhibiting behavior the user considered abnormal.
* The user terminated AGY.
* The user reports that a sandbox environment was enabled.

### Confirmed by Google Documentation

* Antigravity provides a Terminal Sandbox.
* macOS sandboxing uses OS-level Seatbelt / `sandbox-exec` mechanisms.
* Sandboxed commands can write to project folders, temporary directories, and common build caches.
* Antigravity has configurable permission and execution modes.
* Different execution modes provide different levels of automatic approval for file operations.

### Not Yet Established

* Exact files created.
* Exact directories created.
* Exact total bytes generated.
* Exact timestamps.
* Exact AGY process responsible.
* Whether AGY or a spawned subagent generated the data.
* Whether the data was temporary, cached, persistent, project-related, or erroneous.
* Whether the sandbox was functioning according to its documented boundaries.
* Whether a software defect caused the disk growth.
* Whether the behavior corresponds to any previously reported AGY issue.

---

## 13. Requested Investigation

Google Antigravity should investigate whether the reported behavior represents a defect or limitation involving uncontrolled persistent storage growth.

The investigation should specifically determine whether a sandboxed AGY session can:

1. generate extremely large amounts of persistent data;
2. generate repeated session state;
3. create orphaned state after interruption;
4. continuously grow logs or databases;
5. exhaust host disk space without an explicit disk quota;
6. leave large persistent artifacts after the agent terminates.

---

## 14. Evidence Preservation Statement

The affected system should not be cleaned until the relevant files have been identified and documented.

The purpose of this investigation is not to attribute intent.

The purpose is to establish an accurate technical record of:

**what was created, where it was created, when it was created, how much storage it consumed, why it existed, and what component created it.**

---

## 15. Current Conclusion

At this stage, the incident cannot responsibly be attributed to a specific AGY subsystem.

However, the reported scale of storage consumption warrants forensic investigation.

The fact that the user reports operating AGY within a sandbox is particularly relevant because sandboxing addresses execution and filesystem boundaries, while the incident concerns potentially uncontrolled **resource consumption**.

The central technical question is therefore:

> **How could a sandboxed Antigravity CLI session consume approximately 130 GB of host storage, and what data accounted for that consumption?**

That question should be answered from filesystem and AGY telemetry evidence before the affected data is removed.

**Report status: OPEN — Evidence collection required.**

items.title: feat(examples): add automated setup scripts for statusline and title
items.body:
This PR introduces automated `setup.sh` scripts for both the custom `statusline` and the custom terminal `title` examples.

### Problem
Previously, configuring the custom statusline or window title was a manual multi-step process that required:
1. Copying the script from the cloned repository to a global settings directory (so it stays configured even if the repo is deleted/moved).
2. Figuring out the platform-specific config directory (Linux vs macOS vs Windows).
3. Editing `settings.json` manually to set the exact absolute path to the script and enabling the feature.
4. Additionally, some documentation referred to non-existent slash commands like `/statusline enable`.

### Solution
This PR adds two simple scripts:
- `examples/statusline/setup.sh`
- `examples/title/setup.sh`

Running either script will automatically:
1. Detect the platform's settings directory (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/antigravity-cli` on macOS, and `%APPDATA%\\antigravity-cli` on Windows).
2. Copy the corresponding helper script (`statusline.sh` / `title.sh`) there.
3. Automatically update `settings.json` with the correct absolute path using python/jq (safely parsing and inserting/updating JSON keys without breaking other settings).
4. Mark the target script as executable.

It also updates the `README.md` files (in the root and example directories) to present this as the recommended, one-command setup path, while preserving the manual configuration steps for advanced users.

Closes #74

items.body:
## Summary
- Add docs/termux.md with a Termux setup guide for running the Linux ARM64 Antigravity CLI on Android/Termux.
- Link the Termux guide from the README top links and Installation section.

## Why
Termux users can hit several platform compatibility issues when running the Linux ARM64 agy binary directly on Android, including ARM64 VA39/TCMalloc assumptions, Android seccomp blocking faccessat2, glibc libc.so linker-script loading, Termux LD_PRELOAD pollution, DNS resolver discovery, TLS certificate discovery, and shell command hashing.

This guide documents the currently working setup and troubleshooting checks without changing the CLI binary, installer, or runtime behavior for existing platforms.

## Maintainer notes
- This is documentation-only.
- The guide explicitly calls out that the VA39 binary patch is a practical workaround, not a substitute for an official supported build.
- The documented patch script is conservative and warns if expected instruction patterns are missing.
- The guide also lists preferred upstream fixes, such as an official VA39-compatible Linux ARM64 build, runtime allocator configuration, a non-TCMalloc build, or an official Android/Termux-compatible build.

## Validation
- Ran git diff --cached --check before commit.
- No runtime tests were run because this repository currently only contains documentation/assets and this change is docs-only.
